newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Philippines Petron Corp mulls first gas oil export.
newsitem.headline: Philippines Petron Corp mulls first gas oil export.

text.p: Philippines Petron Corp is considering exporting its first gas oil cargo because of an expected surplus in dometic supplies and to take advantage of high international prices, a Petron source said on Thursday.
"It's a good time to sell but we are still looking at it," the source said. "We have not finalised anything yet and it depends on availabilities."

The source said Petron's Bataan refinery is now running at slightly under its full capacity of 165,000 barrels per day (bpd) and the gas oil sale would be finalised if they faced tight ullage in storage.
"It could be a one-off sale of 0.5-percent sulphur gas oil and the sale could be seen in one month," the source said.

The physical gas oil price rallied to a five-year high on Wednesday of $29.70 per barrel when a 220,000-barrel cargo was sold by a European major to a U.S. trader for October 17-21 lifting, free-on-board (fob) Singapore.
The Bataan refinery was expanded by 10,000 bpd last December from its previous 155,000 bpd capacity.
Gas oil comprises 30 percent and kerosene 10 percent of processing capacity. The balance comprises naphtha, gasoline and fuel oil.

Petron used to be a regular buyer of 0.5-percent sulphur gas oil when the National Power Corp (Napocor) was facing severe power shortage in 1993-1994. At that time, Petron imported by tender 300,000 barrels of gas oil a month.
But Petron stopped importing gas oil in 1995 when Napocor gradually switched to fuel oil for power generation. It also uses hydropower, geothermal, coal and some gas oil for generating sources.
Petron bought a cargo of gas oil in April when the Bataan refinery was shut during April/May this year.
The company also exports 10 cargoes of naphtha on a term basis a year and another four to five spot cargoes a year.
